senses.gloss: An extra top gear that lets a car's engine turn slower at highway speed.
examples: The truck drops out of *overdrive* on the long climbs.
At sixty it shifts into *overdrive* and the engine quiets right down.
Older cars had no *overdrive*, so freeway driving was loud.

senses.gloss: The people or things left over because a space cannot hold them all.
examples: The church seated the *overflow* in the basement and piped in the sound.
An *overflow* crowd watched the game from the parking lot.
We rented a second van for the *overflow*.

senses.gloss: An extra period of play added when a game is tied at the end of regulation.
examples: The game went to *overtime* and they lost on a field goal.
She scored twice in *overtime*.
Two of their last three games have gone into *overtime*.

senses.gloss: A higher tone that sounds faintly along with a played note and gives an instrument its color.
examples: The bell's *overtones* hung in the air long after it was struck.
A flute and a violin on the same note differ in their *overtones*.
Tune the string until that ringing *overtone* disappears.

senses.gloss: An approach made to someone in order to open talks or begin a relationship.
examples: The company made *overtures* to a smaller rival about a merger.
He ignored her *overtures* of friendship for months.
Both sides brushed aside the early peace *overtures*.

senses.gloss: Responsibility that a person willingly takes on for a task or a problem.
examples: Somebody needs to take *ownership* of this bug.
She showed real *ownership* of the project from her first week.
The manager keeps asking for more *ownership* from her team.

senses.gloss: One of the small capsules of paint fired from an air gun in the game.
examples: A *paintball* caught him square in the mask.
We went through two bags of *paintballs* in an hour.
The *paintballs* leave a yellow splatter that washes right out.

senses.gloss: An instrument of hinged rods that copies a drawing at a larger or smaller scale.
examples: He used a *pantograph* to enlarge the sketch onto the wall.
The trophy shop still engraves plates with an old *pantograph*.
A *pantograph* traces the shape and redraws it at whatever size you set.

senses.gloss: A person who lives off other people and gives nothing back.
examples: He called his brother-in-law a *parasite* living off the family.
The article painted the whole board as *parasites*.
He'd work two jobs before he'd feel like a *parasite*.

senses.gloss: A writing material made from prepared animal skin, used for documents before paper.
examples: The museum keeps the treaty, written on *parchment*, in a sealed case.
Monks copied whole books onto *parchment* by hand.
The old deed was inked on *parchment* that had gone brown at the edges.

senses.gloss: A short function word, such as 'up' or 'to', that does grammatical work but carries little meaning alone.
examples: In 'give up', the word 'up' is a *particle*, not a preposition.
The *particle* 'to' marks the infinitive.
A phrasal verb is a verb plus a *particle*.

senses.gloss: The dividing of a country into separate states or zones.
examples: The *partition* of India uprooted millions of people.
They argued for *partition* along ethnic lines.
The *partition* left families stranded on opposite sides of a new border.

senses.gloss: Something that gives a person access to a better position or opportunity.
examples: A degree is no longer a *passport* to a good job.
The scholarship was her *passport* out of the mill town.
Solid English is a *passport* to work almost anywhere.

senses.gloss: A thing made up of many different parts that do not fit together neatly.
examples: State privacy rules are a *patchwork* that changes at every border.
From the plane the farmland was a *patchwork* of green and brown.
His coverage is a *patchwork* of three different plans.

senses.gloss: A person's background and record of past achievements.
examples: The new coach arrived with an impressive *pedigree*.
Her academic *pedigree* opened a lot of doors.
Two of the finalists had the same *pedigree*: state school, then a clerkship.
